title: Residential Childcare Worker
description:
Residential Childcare Worker
Children's Residential - Stalybridge SK15
Job Role
A rewarding opportunity to make a genuine difference in the lives of children and young people.
A children's residential home in Stalybridge is looking to recruit caring, reliable and dedicated individuals to help create a safe, supportive and welcoming environment for young people.
Previous experience in residential childcare isn't essential. What's most important is having the right values, emotional resilience and a genuine passion for supporting young people. Full training and development opportunities will be provided.
Responsibilities
You'll be part of a close-knit team helping children feel safe, supported and optimistic about their future. Your responsibilities will include:
Building positive relationships based on trust, consistency and respect.
Supporting daily routines, including school runs, meals, activities and emotional support.
Providing reassurance and being a reliable adult during challenging moments.
Maintaining accurate records of key events and each child's progress.
Promoting education, wellbeing, independence, life skills and positive experiences.
Helping to create a warm, welcoming environment where children feel at home.
Requirements
This opportunity could suit someone who:
Has experience in care, education, youth work or a similar setting, although this isn't essential.
Has strong interpersonal skills, emotional resilience and a natural ability to build relationships.
Can remain calm and consistent during challenging situations.
Is willing to learn about supporting children who have experienced trauma and adversity.
Is comfortable working independently when required and following structured routines.
Holds a full UK driving licence and has access to a car (essential).
A Level 3 qualification in Residential Childcare or Level 4 qualification in Children, Young People and Families is desirable but not essential. Those without the relevant qualification will be supported through a fully funded Level 4 Children, Young People and Families Practitioner qualification.
Salary, Benefits & Development
13.50 per hour.
1,000 welcome bonus ( 500 upon successful completion of induction and 500 upon successful completion of probation).
2 days on, 4 days off rota, averaging approximately 10 working days per month.
Paid overtime at 14.50 per hour.
Sleep-ins available as required, paid at 75 per night.
Fully funded Level 4 qualification.
Structured induction, ongoing training, regular supervision and coaching.
Opportunities for career progression and further development.
Cash health plan, employee recognition awards, crisis fund and long-service recognition.
Two additional days of annual leave each year, increasing to three after your first year and four after your second year.
Rota pattern designed to support a healthy work-life balance.
Additional Information
The 1,000 welcome bonus is subject to repayment on a pro-rata basis if an employee voluntarily leaves or is dismissed for misconduct within their first 12 months.
All successful applicants will be subject to safer recruitment and pre-employment checks. A charge of up to 74.70 may initially apply for right-to-work checks, ID checks and DBS applications, where applicable. These costs are refundable following successful completion of induction.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Location: Cheadle

Salary: £12.71 per hour

Contract Type: Zero Hour

Shift Patterns: Long days, nights & sleepovers (must be willing to work all shifts, not just nights)

We are currently looking to recruit experienced Support Workers to work within a variety of environments including Supported Living, Residential Services, Specialist Units and Private Hospitals as part of our established health and social care agency.

The Role:

As a Support Worker at Pin Point Health your main duties will include:
- Administering medication
- Assisting with daily living and domestic duties
- Developing positive working relationships with the multi-disciplinary team
- Ensuring that the health, safety and welfare of clients is always protected
- Maintaining accurate and up to date reports such as support plans
- Completing all necessary administrative duties
- Maintaining regular communication with the Service Manager
- Respect the individuality and confidentiality of each client
- Build and maintain relationships with service users and their families.

The Person:

The following experience and characteristics are considered essential to the role:
- A minimum of 6-12 months experience within a healthcare environment, preferably supporting clients with learning disabilities, autism, challenging behaviour or mental health needs.
- The ability to be patient & calm under pressure
- Easily adaptable to new environments
- Reliable & trustworthy
- Eligible to work in the UK
- Access to your own transport is desirable, however this is not essential
- Flexible to work within multiple environments on a weekly basis dependant on the requirements of our clients.

The Package:
You will have access to the following benefits as part of the role of Support Worker with Pin Point Health:
- Full time and Part time work available
- Holiday allowance accrued as you work
- FREE annual mandatory training
- "Refer a friend" scheme that pays £50.00 per candidate referred
- A competitive hourly rate with further enhancements for Bank Holidays
- Access to our online staff portal to manage your availability and work assignments
- The opportunity to work within a wide range of different environments on a weekly basis

The Company:
Pin Point Health work in partnership with a wide range of care providers in order to deliver high quality, consistent and reliable staffing solutions.

We offer part time, full time and contract positions to our team of experienced Support Worker s within a wide range of different environments across the UK.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Learning Support Assistant - SEMH (Secondary SEND School)
Stockport
450 - 550 per week
Full-time Term-time only Long-term role with permanent opportunities
Are you passionate about supporting young people with additional needs? Do you have the resilience and adaptability to thrive in a specialist SEMH environment?
We are currently recruiting for a Learning Support Assistant to join a well-resourced and highly supportive secondary SEND school in Stockport. The school has an excellent reputation, outstanding provisions for its students, and a welcoming, knowledgeable team who are committed to making a real difference.
This role will primarily involve working within the school's SEMH provision, supporting pupils who may become deregulated and require additional emotional and behavioural support.
The Role:
Supporting students with SEMH needs on a 1:1 and small group basis
Working within a specialist provision and across the wider school as required
Supporting pupils through periods of deregulation in a calm and consistent manner
Adapting quickly to changing situations and student needs
Promoting engagement, emotional regulation, and positive outcomes
About You:
Passionate about supporting vulnerable young people to reach their full potential
Resilient, patient, and confident managing behaviours that challenge
Flexible and quick-thinking in a dynamic school environment
A strong team player with a proactive approach
Ideal experience:
Residential care / children's homes
Foster care or family support
Youth work, mentoring, or coaching
Sports, behaviour support, or alternative provision settings
What's on offer:
450- 550 per week (depending on experience)
Full-time, term-time only role starting in September
Long-term opportunity with potential for a permanent contract
A fantastic school environment with excellent resources and support
Opportunity to work alongside an experienced and dedicated team
This is a rewarding opportunity for someone who wants to make a genuine impact in a school that truly invests in both its students and staff.
Apply today to be considered for this role.
Aspire People Limited provides services as an Education Agency and an Education Employment Business. Aspire People is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of pupils and expects every candidate to share this commitment. Placements are subject, to appropriate Child Protection screening, including checks with former employers and the Disclosure and Barring Checks.

title: Care Assistant - Care Home
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Care Assistant at Barchester, you'll play a vital role in helping our residents enjoy each day to the fullest. Providing both practical support and meaningful companionship, you'll make a genuine difference to the lives of the people you care for.

In this role, you'll:
- Support residents with daily living activities and personal care
- Help residents with food and drink throughout the day
- Build positive relationships and provide companionship
- Follow individual care plans and support resident wellbeing
- Spend valuable one-to-one time with residents
- Encourage independence while promoting dignity and respect
- Work as part of a caring team to deliver high-quality support

No two days are ever the same, making this a rewarding opportunity to use your skills, develop your experience and make a real impact every day.

ABOUT YOU

We're looking for someone who is kind, compassionate and committed to delivering excellent care.

To join us as a Care Assistant, you'll have:
- Experience caring for older people
- A positive, can-do attitude
- Excellent communication and people skills
- A warm, empathetic and respectful approach
- A genuine passion for supporting others

Above all, you'll have the compassion and dedication needed to provide the highest standard of care and support. In return, we'll give you all the training and development you need to succeed.

REWARDS PACKAGE

In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus a sector-leading benefits and rewards package, including:
- Free training and development opportunities
- Access to wellbeing and support tools
- A range of retail discounts and savings
- Unlimited referrals through our Refer a Friend bonus scheme
- Employee of the Month recognition
- Long Service Awards
- Career development opportunities within one of the UK's leading care providers

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality of care you'd expect for your own loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

Our Care Home Manager is always happy to welcome you into the home for an informal chat, so feel free to pop in and find out more about working at Barchester.
